textArea.b: The wedge (now) is smaller than the vision (later)
VISION (LATER): any doctor who needs a family history, one specialty at a time

g.textArea: Any doctor who needs a family history, one specialty at a time: the rest of NYC's ~20 cardiology groups → larger groups → genetics and lipid clinics → primary care wellness visits. US independent cardiology alone: 7,699 cardiologists, $3.8M a year at $500. Markets beyond it are not yet sized. (slide 9)

3 independent NYC cardiology groups. Why cardiology first: its guidelines count grandparents, aunts and uncles, by side and age.
Goal: 4 in 10 invited new patients have a reviewed page in the chart before visit one. (slide 9)
1. Pilot (from about Jan 2027)
Trigger to move on: ≥ 40% completion and ≥ 1 annual contract
NYC's 285–320 independent cardiologists [S27] are worth $142–160k a year at $500: a pilot market, not a business.

Why cardiology first. Its criteria need which relative, which side and what age, out to grandparents, aunts and uncles [76][77][72]; Medicare's wellness visit requires, at minimum, only parents, siblings and children [104]. And one practice manager can say yes. In our wedge scoring (team judgment before any buyer call), independent NYC cardiology scores 21 of 30 and primary care wellness visits 19; if access were 2 instead of 4, primary care would tie, so the five manager calls decide. Decision rule: if fewer than 3 of 5 cardiology managers name a budget owner by Oct 23, run the same five calls with primary care practice managers. Our ER interviewee pointed to primary care as the bigger user of family history (ID010, note); it is our expansion market. Any visit can use it today; only cardiology has clinician criteria.

2. Fill the city, then larger groups: The rest of the ~19–20 NYC groups; large independent and PE groups (CVAUSA [102])
Trigger to move on: 10+ paying practices; a repeatable onboarding playbook

3. Health-system specialty clinics: Cardiogenetics and lipid programs [S47][S48][S49]
Trigger to move on: Pilot outcome data; a clinician champion; a production Epic app [5]

4. Primary care: Practices running Medicare Annual Wellness Visits [104]
Trigger to move on: General question set built (Oct 2026); criteria only after a clinician signs; help flows for older users [90]

Side door (any time): Patients whose practice isn't a customer
Trigger to move on: None; free, prints a page

Market check. The 7,699 are US cardiologists in organizations of 100 or fewer clinicians, a proxy that includes some hospital practices [99]: $3.8M a year at $500, or $9.1–13.8M at the higher monthly prices modeled in Step 5.3 (A4). Markets beyond independent cardiology are not yet sized. Each step reuses the tree, relative links and sources; a new specialty adds its own questions and clinician criteria, signed off by that specialty (cardiology's are built, not yet signed off; other visits get a general question set, no criteria).

• Who: 3 independent NYC cardiology groups, 2–10 cardiologists, cardiology at least half the clinicians, a manager with a software budget, about 20+ adult new patients a month, an EHR that accepts a PDF, willing to sign a BAA. Mix: different EHRs, at least one outside Manhattan, at least one with a prevention or lipid focus.
• Pool: 39 NYC organizations with 2+ independent cardiologists; 22 are cardiology-focused, and about 19–20 remain once hospital-linked groups are removed (team analysis of the CMS file [S27]; check each by phone).
• Why not solo practices first: too few new patients for a 12-week pilot to read a completion rate (at ~21 a month per cardiologist, assumption, a 3-cardiologist group sends ~60 invites a month; at 60 invites a 40% rate is known to about ±12 points).
• First offer ("founding practice pilot"): one link added to new-patient paperwork; one page per patient before the visit; set-up in one call; baseline staff-minute count; help line; week-6 and week-12 reports. $1,000 flat for 12 weeks, credited in full to year one; then $500 per cardiologist per year. BAA first, no patient data before it. No auto-renew. Never priced per referral or new patient.
• Users: all adult new patients (one link in the new-patient paperwork; a practice can't easily filter by referral reason); value is sharpest for palpitations, fainting, chest pain and high cholesterol.
• Earliest start: about January 2027, after we form a company, the BAA stack and insurance are live, counsel has reviewed the BAA template and privacy policy, a cardiologist has signed the rule table and the pilot backend runs (critical path in Step 5.2). Letters of intent can be signed now.
• Metric zero (by Oct 23): 5 practice-manager conversations; 3 name the budget owner and accept $500/yr in principle; 1 signs a non-binding letter of intent naming a target start month.
• Pilot metric 1: of invited adult new patients whose first visit falls in pilot weeks 2–12, the share with a patient-reviewed summary in the chart before that visit. Target ≥ 40%, read at week 6 and week 12. On day 1 the practice also texts patients who are already booked, so the early weeks have visits (the average new-patient wait is 33 days [S2], so patients invited at booking in week 1 are seen around week 5). Checks at week 6: clinician opens it and rates it ≥ 4/5, scan < 60 s; ≥ 25% of patients get one relative's answer; staff minutes, baseline vs pilot (report, don't promise); ≤ 2 specific alerts per summary.
• Go/no-go at week 12: go if pilot metric 1 ≥ 40% and ≥ 1 of 3 practices signs an annual contract. High completion but nobody pays: switch buyers (health-system cardiogenetics or lipid clinics, or primary care). Completion under 20%: fix the patient flow before selling more.
